papers.title_in_file: Classification and emergence of quantum spin liquids in chiral Rydberg models
papers.version_note: arXiv:2303.12829v2 (8 Aug 2023); the text layer holds the preprint once, 13 pages; figure panels and tables print as garbled text, so figure values are named in anchors only.
papers.what_it_is: A parton (projective symmetry group) classification of chiral spin liquids on the honeycomb lattice, tested against exact diagonalization and DMRG of a chiral Rydberg-atom model at 1/2 and 1/4 density.

assertions.value: The authors report a classification of fermionic chiral spin liquids with U(1) global symmetry, built by parton construction on the honeycomb lattice, that includes six distinct classes of gapped quantum spin liquids.
quotes: We classify all possible fermionic chiral spin liquids with U(1) global symmetry using parton construction on the honeycomb lattice.
The resulting classification includes six distinct classes of gapped quantum spin liquids
assertions.certainty_reason: A classification result stated in the abstract; the derivation is in Section III and Appendix B.

assertions.value: The authors state that an earlier honeycomb-lattice projective symmetry group classification finds 160 algebraic PSGs, and that without time-reversal symmetry the number of classes reduces to 24.
assertions.anchor: Section III, p.3; Appendix B, Table I, p.9
quotes: where 160 different algebraic PSG's are found.
Thus, we find that the number of different classes of algebraic PSG is reduced to 24
assertions.certainty_reason: Count of 160 is cited from Lu and Ran; the reduction to 24 is the authors' own derivation.

assertions.value: The authors state that restricting to ansatze with nonzero mean-field amplitudes on nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor links leaves 6 distinct ansatze.
quotes: Given the model that we study, we focus on those ansa¨tze that have nonzero mean-field amplitudes on the NN and NNN links. This leaves 6 distinct ansa¨tze
assertions.certainty_reason: Scope of the variational search, stated by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that the classification rules out a gapless Dirac spectrum, because the Dirac spin liquid submanifold preserves time-reversal symmetry, which the Hamiltonian breaks explicitly.
quotes: it rules out the possibility of gapless Dirac spectrum
However, this DSL ansatz submanifold preserves time-reversal, which is explicitly broken by our Hamiltonian.
This excludes the possibility of a DSL being stabilized in chiral systems such as our model.
assertions.certainty_reason: Argued by symmetry in the text; no formal theorem statement is given.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing Wen, Wilczek and Zee, that such chiral mean-field states are stable beyond mean-field treatment because the mean-field gauge fluctuations are gapped out by the Chern-Simons mechanism.
quotes: Such chiral mean-field states are stable beyond mean-field treatment, as the mean-field gauge fluctuations are gapped out by the Chern-Simons mechanism
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work (Ref. 44).

assertions.value: The authors report, from earlier work, that at small g the model is a Bose-Einstein condensate and at large g it shows spiral order, with an intermediate phase between them that shows no clear order, is believed to be a spin liquid candidate, and whose true nature remained unclear.
quotes: The intermediate phase between 0.4 ≲ g ≲ 0.9, shows no clear order, and it is believed to be a candidate for a spin liquid.
its true nature remains unclear, also due to hard-to-interpret spectral properties.
assertions.certainty_reason: Prior result from Ohler et al. (Ref. 25) restated as background.

assertions.value: The authors set up an effective hard-core boson model on the honeycomb lattice with nearest-neighbor hopping, density-assisted next-nearest-neighbor chiral hopping and nearest-neighbor interaction, with g = w2/(2µ), valid in the regime where the internal state is adiabatically eliminated and hopping is truncated at nearest-neighbor distance; the Hamiltonian has U(1) symmetry from particle-number conservation.
quotes: where J = tb and g = w2/(2µ).
The Hamiltonian has U(1) symmetry related to particle-number conservation.
Hereafter, we set the energy scale to J = 1.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own model in Section II.

assertions.value: The authors report that, by maximizing the overlap with the exact ground state on a 16-site cluster at g = 0.7, ansatz no. 1 has the largest overlap at 1/2 density, with amplitude ratios u2iτ0 /u1τ0 = −0.31 and u2iτ3 /uτ10 = −0.1.
quotes: The optimization is performed on a 16-site cluster at g = 0.7.
We find that the ansatz with the largest overlap with the ground state at 1/2density is ansatz no. 1
assertions.certainty_reason: A numerical optimization result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Gutzwiller-projected ansatz has a gapped mean-field state and a two-fold topological degeneracy on a torus; the overlap matrix of the four twisted-boundary states has rank 2 within a numerical accuracy on the order of 10−2.
quotes: The topological nature of such CSL is manifested by the two-fold topological degeneracy of states on a torus.
We find that the rank of the overlap matrix is 2, within a numerical accuracy on the order of 10−2.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical evidence on finite clusters.

assertions.value: The authors report a many-body Chern number C = 2 for the spinon wavefunction, computed on a D = 24 twist mesh, and divide the result by 4 because the spinon twist range corresponds to a larger twist range for the spin operators, giving a fractionalized Chern number C = 1/2 per state.
quotes: We have obtained C = 2, with the Berry curvature for D = 24 is shown in Fig. 3b.
must be divided by 4.
of the spin wavefunction is fractionalized C = 1/2 per state.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result on one cluster.

assertions.value: The authors state that the CSL at 1/2 density is a new phase, with a dispersive single-particle band at integer filling, an interaction-driven topological phase generated from a trivial band insulator, which approaches based on flat bands would miss.
quotes: the CSL at 1/2 density is a new phase which corresponds to integer filling of the single-particle band
this CSL has a dispersive band (see Fig. 3a)
this CSL is inevitably missed by previous approaches relying on the identification of flat bands
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own claim of novelty.

assertions.value: The authors report that the ground-state overlap with the two topological states remains large in the intermediate phase with increasing system size, and that on a 32-site cluster the ground state is not in the rotation-neutral sector yet one of the two topological states lies in the same nontrivial rotation sector.
quotes: It can be seen that the overlap remains large in the middle phase with increasing system size
on a 32-site cluster, we find that the ground state in the intermediate phase is not in the rotation-neutral sector.
one of the two topological states is in the same nontrivial rotation sector as the ground state of the Hamiltonian
assertions.certainty_reason: Exact diagonalization on finite clusters; overlap values are in Fig. 4a only.

assertions.value: The authors report that at quarter density the CSL phase of the effective model emerges in a narrow range around g = 0.2, that ansatz no. 4 gives large overlaps, and that the overlap reaches 0.96 at the largest system size considered, L = 40.
quotes: we found that the CSL phase emerges in a narrow range around g = 0.2.
We obtain large overlaps with the ansatz no. 4 at small-size clusters in the CSL phase.
reaching 0.96 at the largest system size we considered, L = 40.
assertions.certainty_reason: Exact diagonalization overlap on finite clusters.

assertions.value: The authors report that at quarter density the approximate two-fold ground-state degeneracy is clearly visible in the ED spectra even on small clusters, and both nearly degenerate states have huge overlaps with the optimal wavefunction ansatz.
quotes: the approximate two-fold degeneracy can already be observed clearly from the ED spectra, even on small-size clusters.
both of the nearly-degenerate states have huge overlaps with the optimal wavefunction ansatz.
assertions.certainty_reason: Exact diagonalization result on small clusters.

assertions.value: The authors report that no approximate two-fold degeneracy appears in the ED spectra at half density, which they attribute to finite-size effects; at g = 0.7 the ground state has the highest overlap and one low-lying state a modest overlap, while at g = 0.1 the overlaps show no clear pattern.
assertions.anchor: Section IV, Fig. 5, p.5; Appendix C, p.10
quotes: we observe no approximate two-fold degeneracy in the ED spectra, which would have been expected in a CSL.
Nevertheless, this can be attributed to finite-size effects
at g = 0.7, we observe that the overlap is highest for the ground state, and that there is a low-lying state with a modest overlap.
at g = 0.1, the overlaps do not exhibit any clear pattern for each system size.
assertions.certainty_reason: Finite-cluster exact diagonalization; the finite-size explanation is the authors' hypothesis.
assertions.reader_inference: The missing degeneracy at 1/2 density is a weakness in the evidence for a CSL there; the paper itself leans on overlaps instead.

assertions.value: The authors report from ED on a small cluster that the gap to the first excited state may become very small at isolated twist points while the second gap and the charge gap remain wide open, which they contrast with the expected Dirac spin liquid behavior where all gaps vanish.
quotes: while the first gap may become very small at some isolated points in twist space, the second gap and charge gap remain wide open.
This contrasts with the expected behavior of a DSL, where all gaps would exhibit a vanishing behavior with respect to twist angles
assertions.certainty_reason: Exact diagonalization on finite clusters.

assertions.value: The authors propose that, for the CSL at n = 1/2 density, the two ground states lie in the same k = (0, 0) momentum sector, so their flow under flux insertion appears as an avoided crossing, which they offer as the explanation of the apparent vanishing of the first gap seen in earlier work.
quotes: In the case of CSL at n = 1/2 density, the two ground states live in the same k = (0, 0) momentum sector.
the flow between these ground states manifests as an avoided crossing.
assertions.certainty_reason: An interpretation offered by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the CSL phase at half density, even in small systems, the Kitaev-Preskill topological entanglement entropy from the exact ground state is finite and close to the value expected for a fractional quantum Hall state, and they caution that finite volume effects prevent a clear interpretation as a signature of topological order.
assertions.anchor: Section VI, Fig. 7, p.5; footnote 59, p.13
quotes: In the CSL phase, even in small systems, the computed γ is finite, and close
the finite volume effects prevent a clear interpretation of this data as a striking signature of topological order
assertions.certainty_reason: Small-cluster ED result that the authors themselves caveat.

assertions.value: The authors report from DMRG on cylinders that nearest-neighbor edge currents in the intermediate phase are significantly larger than in the neighboring phases, and that substantial counter-propagating nearest-neighbor edge currents appear only in the CSL phase and vanish in the bulk.
quotes: in the intermediate phase are significantly larger compared to those in the neighboring phases.
substantial counter-propagating NN edge currents manifests only in the CSL phase that vanish in the bulk.
assertions.certainty_reason: DMRG result on finite cylinders of periodic width 4.

assertions.value: The authors report signs of another intermediate phase with non-zero edge currents for 0.25 ≲ g ≲ 0.4 between the BEC phase and the CSL, in which reflection times time-reversal symmetry is spontaneously broken, with a two-fold degenerate ground-state manifold; they state its full characterization is beyond the scope of the work.
quotes: Notice that Fig. 1c also exhibits signatures of another intermediate phase with non-zero edge currents for 0.25 ≲ g ≲ 0.4.
While its full characterization is beyond the scope of this work
In the new intermediate phase, reflection × time-reversal symmetry gets spontaneously broken, and the total edge current becomes finite
clearly indicates two-fold degenerate ground-state manifold in this new unknown phase.
assertions.certainty_reason: Preliminary DMRG and ED findings the authors label preliminary.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the additional phase the overlap with the Dirac spin liquid wavefunction, obtained by setting the next-nearest-neighbor terms to zero, is remarkably close to the optimal overlap, and they suggest as one possible scenario that the DSL wavefunction describes the critical wavefunction at the BEC-to-new-phase transition.
quotes: Indeed, the overlap with the DSL wavefunction (blue line), which is obtained by setting the NNN interactions to zero, is remarkably close with the optimal overlap.
One possible scenario to explain this observation is that the DSL wavefunction describes the critical wavefunction at the transition from the BEC phase to the unknown phase.
assertions.certainty_reason: Overlap on one 24-site cluster; the critical-wavefunction reading is a stated possibility only.

assertions.value: The authors state that the DMRG runs use cylinders of periodic width LPBC = 4 (8 lattice sites), with MPS bond dimension in the range χ ∈ [2000, 4000] and cut-off errors of the order of 10−5 to 10−7.
quotes: periodic boundary conditions along the one axis with length LPBC = 4 (8 lattice sites)
taken in the range χ ∈ [2000, 4000] resulting in cut-off errors of the order of 10−5 to 10−7 depending on the system parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own simulation setup in Appendix D.

assertions.value: The authors report that the iMPS transfer matrix spectrum shows no signature of Dirac cone behavior and is consistent with a Chern insulator, while a sharp jump in one charge sector near a twist of 0.9π may be a numerical artifact of finite bond dimension.
quotes: the results do not show any signatures of a Dirac cone behavior
the transfer matrix spectrum is consistent with a Chern insulator
we see a sharp jump in the spectrum around θPBC ≈ 0.9π which could be a numerical artifact of finite iMPS bond dimension
assertions.certainty_reason: iDMRG result at one bond dimension on one cylinder geometry.

assertions.value: The authors report from ED on periodic clusters of 24 and 28 sites that the effective model hosts a CSL regime for both truncation distances, that extending the hopping range shifts the CSL phase to the right and changes the nature of the large-g phase, and that the gap converges uniformly in g to the µ = ∞ curve as µ grows, though this is not enough to unequivocally identify a CSL at finite µ.
quotes: numerical evidence from exact diagonalization on periodic clusters of 24 and 28 sites
it shifts to the right the CSL phase and it changes the nature of the large-g phase
We observe convergence (uniformly in g) to the µ = ∞ curve
to unequivocally identify a CSL phase at finite
assertions.certainty_reason: ED on small clusters, reported with an explicit caveat.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Appendix A analysis only probes the validity of the adiabatic elimination at different hopping truncations, and does not probe the stability of a CSL phase at finite µ and longer hopping range in a generic filling sector.
quotes: does not aim at probing the stability of a CSL phase at finite µ and RT > 1 in a generic filling sector.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of its own scope in Appendix A.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that Gutzwiller-projected parton CSL wavefunctions capture the intermediate disordered phase in chiral Rydberg atom arrays and resolve the previously unclear nature of the intermediate phase found in Ref. 25.
quotes: We show that the CSL wavefunctions constructed from the Gutzwiller-projected parton wavefunctions are able to capture the intermediate disordered phase in chiral Rydberg atom arrays.
our results resolve the previously unclear nature of the intermediate phase found in Ref. [25].
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' conclusion, resting on finite-cluster evidence.
assertions.reader_inference: The text elsewhere admits missing two-fold degeneracy at 1/2 density and finite-size caveats on entanglement entropy, so resolve is stronger than the evidence shown.
